findings.observed: The page states, verbatim: "Support verified temples and gaushalas across India." and carries a trust badge reading "Every cause verified by our team". The fourth gaushala cause listed directly under that badge, with a live "Donate" CTA, is an unvetted record: name "saharanpur", location "saharanpur", description "skkss", address "ssdwdqe", totalCows 1. The API confirms approved:true and returns donationCauseId d56b9b2a-f520-4c34-8dc6-93cd07a9116e, so it resolves to a real donee that /donations/create-order would accept — real money can be routed to it.
findings.expected: Either the record is unapproved and removed from the public directory, or the page stops asserting that every listed cause is verified. A donations page taking real money must not publish a verification claim that its own listings contradict.
findings.evidence: Page text: 'Support verified temples and gaushalas across India. Every donation gets a numbered PDF receipt by email. Razorpay-secured payments.' plus badge 'Every cause verified by our team'. Cause card text: '1+ cows  saharanpur  saharanpur  skkss  Donate'. API GET /gaushala/03edd2ff-4479-48f3-9ad1-6940e5558a4d -> 200 {"gaushala":{"id":"03edd2ff-4479-48f3-9ad1-6940e5558a4d","name":"saharanpur","location":"saharanpur","description":"skkss","address":"ssdwdqe","totalCows":1,"approved":true,...,"donationCauseId":"d56b9b2a-f520-4c34-8dc6-93cd07a9116e"}}. The same record also appears on /gaushala under the badge 'Reviewed Gaushalas — Approved before they are listed' and has its own live page at /gaushala/profile/03edd2ff-... (200, title 'saharanpur — Gau Seva | Darshya'). Note: the payment mechanics are not themselves broken — money would reach the donee the page names. What is wrong is the verification claim and the fact that an obviously junk record passed approval into a live money path.

findings.observed: Any :id that is not a valid uuid and is not one of the gs_00x fixtures returns 500 {"error":"InternalServerError","message":"Something went wrong on our end.","code":"INTERNAL_ERROR"}. Reproduced on 5/5 non-uuid inputs on the public route (__ct_nonexistent_zzz, abc, gs_999, a space, an emoji string) and 2/2 on the authenticated portal route. A well-formed but nonexistent uuid correctly returns 404 on both routes, which isolates the cause to the id format rather than to the lookup.
findings.expected: 404 (or 400) — the same as for a well-formed nonexistent uuid.
findings.evidence: GET /gaushala/__ct_nonexistent_zzz -> 500; /gaushala/abc -> 500; /gaushala/gs_999 -> 500; /gaushala/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 -> 404 'Gaushala not found.'; GET /gaushala-portal/cows/abc -> 500 while /gaushala-portal/cows/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 -> 404 'Cow not found'. Likely source: apps/api/src/routes/gaushala.ts:29-31 falls through to prisma.gaushalaProfile.findFirst({where:{approved:true,OR:[{id},{userId:id}]}}) with no uuid guard on the path param, so Postgres rejects the cast. The public route needs no authentication, so this is reachable by any visitor or crawler; the web layer masks it with its own 404 page, but the API returns 500 and it will show in error rates.

blocked.reason: Not verifiable within the brief's rules. Per SEC-02 step 4 (apps/web/lib/auth-context.tsx:421-424) the access token is no longer written to any JS-readable store, and the API's darshya_session cookie is host-only for api.darshya.online, so a session cannot be injected into a browser from the cached token. Establishing one requires POST /auth/login, which the brief forbids. Over plain HTTP these pages SSR only a loading skeleton. The API behind every one of them was verified directly and returns correct empty shapes.

Not attempted, by judgement rather than by rule. Creating a QA- cow or volunteer was permitted, but the gaushala account has no GaushalaProfile (dashboard returns profile:null), so PATCH /profile would have created the account's first record — a named entry in the public gaushala directory that then appears as a live donation cause. Given finding gaushala-donations-1 is precisely about junk records reaching that directory, adding one during the audit was the wrong trade. Read paths and the full authz matrix were covered instead.
